    /** Cross-process locking and atomic JSON helpers for catalog writers. */
    import { closeSync, fsyncSync, openSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, renameSync } from 'node:fs';
    import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';
    import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
    
    const LOCK_HELPER = fileURLToPath(new URL('./catalog_flock.py', import.meta.url));
    // Wave 7 runs 8 concurrent generators against a 24MB cookbook.json. A writer
    // killed mid-hold (SIGTERM from a session teardown, OOM) used to leave the
    // lock directory behind; the mtime-only staleness check then forced every
    // sibling to wait LOCK_STALE_MS (10min) while the acquire deadline was only
    // 120s — so one dead batch took down the other three. Break on owner-PID
    // liveness first, and give a live-but-slow holder a generous deadline.
    const LOCK_DEADLINE_MS = Number(process.env.CATALOG_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS ?? 900_000);
    
    // Python and JS catalog writers share the same persistent flock inode.
    // Deploy together with writers stopped: legacy directory locks cannot mix.
    export async function withFileLock(lockPath, fn) {
      const seconds = (Number.isFinite(LOCK_DEADLINE_MS) ? LOCK_DEADLINE_MS : 900_000) / 1000;
      const holder = spawn('python3', ['-u', LOCK_HELPER, lockPath, String(seconds)],
        { stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'] });
      let stderr = '';
      holder.stderr.on('data', chunk => { stderr += chunk; });
      holder.stdin.on('error', () => {}); // exit-before-release must not emit an unhandled EPIPE
      const closed = new Promise(resolve => {
        holder.once('error', () => resolve(-1));
        holder.once('close', code => resolve(code));
      });
      try {
        await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
          let text = '';
          holder.stdout.on('data', chunk => {
            text += chunk;
            if (text.includes('locked\n')) resolve();
          });
          holder.once('error', reject);
          holder.once('close', () => reject(new Error(`catalog lock failed: ${stderr}`)));
        });
        return await fn();
      } finally {
        // EOF releases the helper's lock, also on parent death (no stale owner).
        holder.stdin.end();
        await closed;
      }
    }
    
    // 2026-09-08 (VOCAL-LANGUAGE-NORMALIZATION): canonical 7 creative values.
    // Any write through this lock must coerce vocalLanguage to the closed set,
    // so seed scripts and concurrent wave writers cannot reintroduce drift.
    const CREATIVE_VOCAL_LANGUAGES = new Set([
      'instrumental',
      'english',
      'english-lyrics',
      'invented-phonetic',
      'latin-fake',
      'gibberish-anime',
      'japanese',
    ]);
    function normalizeVocalLanguage(raw, instrumental) {
      if (instrumental) return 'instrumental';
      if (raw == null) return 'english';
      const v = String(raw).trim().toLowerCase();
      if (!v) return 'english';
      if (v === 'none') return 'english';
      if (v === 'instrumental') return 'english';
      if (CREATIVE_VOCAL_LANGUAGES.has(v)) return v;
      return 'english';
    }
    function normalizeCooksVocalLangs(cooks) {
      if (!Array.isArray(cooks)) return;
      for (const c of cooks) {
        if (!c?.recipe) continue;
        const before = c.recipe.vocalLanguage;
        const normalized = normalizeVocalLanguage(before, c.recipe.instrumental);
        if (before !== normalized) c.recipe.vocalLanguage = normalized;
      }
    }
    
    export function readJson(path) {
      return JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, 'utf8'));
    }
    
    export function atomicWriteJson(path, value) {
      const tmp = `${path}.tmp-${process.pid}-${Date.now()}`;
      writeFileSync(tmp, JSON.stringify(value, null, 2) + '\n', 'utf8');
      const fd = openSync(tmp, 'r');
      try { fsyncSync(fd); } finally { closeSync(fd); }
      renameSync(tmp, path);
    }
    
    function clone(value) {
      return JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));
    }
    
    /** Merge this process's changed cook/song records onto the latest disk copy. */
    export function mergeCatalogChanges(base, current, disk) {
      // Normalize in-memory sources so stale `base` copies do not resurrect drift
      // when a concurrent writer merges (wave 7 runs 8 workers). Without this,
      // a worker whose base still has `spanish` would see current==base and
      // skip, but disk merge would keep the stale drift alive.
      normalizeCooksVocalLangs(base?.cooks);
      normalizeCooksVocalLangs(current?.cooks);
      const merged = { ...disk };
      for (const key of ['cooks', 'songs']) {
        const baseById = new Map((base[key] ?? []).map((item) => [item.id, item]));
        const currentById = new Map((current[key] ?? []).map((item) => [item.id, item]));
        const diskItems = [...(disk[key] ?? [])];
        const diskIndex = new Map(diskItems.map((item, index) => [item.id, index]));
        for (const [id, item] of currentById) {
          if (JSON.stringify(baseById.get(id)) === JSON.stringify(item)) continue;
          const next = clone(item);
          if (diskIndex.has(id)) diskItems[diskIndex.get(id)] = next;
          else {
            diskIndex.set(id, diskItems.length);
            diskItems.push(next);
          }
        }
        merged[key] = diskItems;
      }
      normalizeCooksVocalLangs(merged.cooks);
      return merged;
    }
    
    export async function saveCatalogMerge(path, base, current) {
      return withFileLock(`${path}.lock`, async () => {
        const disk = readJson(path);
        const merged = mergeCatalogChanges(base, current, disk);
        merged.updatedAt = current.updatedAt ?? new Date().toISOString();
        atomicWriteJson(path, merged);
        return merged;
      });
    }
    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    """Shared Linux catalog lock. Persistent inode: never unlink the .flock file.
    
    Legacy .lock directories are no longer synchronization primitives. Deploy all
    writers together while stopped; old and new lock protocols must not overlap.
    The OS releases ownership on process death; no PID/mtime reclamation races.
    CLI handshake holds the lock until stdin closes (including parent death).
    """
    import fcntl
    from pathlib import Path
    import sys
    import time
    from contextlib import contextmanager
    
    
    @contextmanager
    def catalog_lock(legacy_path, timeout=120):
        path = Path(str(legacy_path) + '.flock')
        with path.open('a') as handle:
            deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
            while True:
                try:
                    fcntl.flock(handle, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
                    break
                except BlockingIOError:
                    if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                        raise TimeoutError(f'catalog lock timeout: {path}')
                    time.sleep(0.05)
            try:
                yield
            finally:
                fcntl.flock(handle, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
    
    
    if __name__ == '__main__':
        with catalog_lock(sys.argv[1], float(sys.argv[2])):
            print('locked', flush=True)
            sys.stdin.buffer.read()

    #!/usr/bin/env bun
    // bun:test-registered version of the catalog-lock regression test. The
    // previous top-level script printed "PASSED" but `bun test` collected 0
    // tests because it never used the `test()` API. This file now does both:
    // it can still be executed directly (`bun scripts/catalog-lock.test.mjs`)
    // and `bun test` will pick it up and report counts.
    //
    // Note: `bun test` runs each test in its own scope, so the temp dir and
    // fixture file are created in `beforeAll` (per worker) rather than at
    // module top-level. The standalone-script path recreates the same setup
    // in an IIFE.
    import { describe, test, expect, beforeAll, afterAll } from 'bun:test';
    import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, rmSync, writeFileSync, readFileSync, existsSync } from 'node:fs';
    import { join } from 'node:path';
    import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
    import { saveCatalogMerge, withFileLock } from './catalog-lock.mjs';
    
    let root;
    let path;
    let base;
    
    describe('catalog lock', () => {
      beforeAll(() => {
        root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'ai-auto-music-lock-'));
        path = join(root, 'cookbook.json');
        base = {
          version: 1,
          cooks: [{ id: 'cook-a', name: 'A' }],
          songs: [{ id: 'song-a', cookId: 'cook-a', title: 'A' }]
        };
        writeFileSync(path, JSON.stringify(base));
      });
    
      afterAll(() => {
        if (root && existsSync(root)) rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true });
      });
    
      test('concurrent saves merge (no last-write-wins loss)', async () => {
        const left = structuredClone(base);
        left.cooks[0].name = 'A changed';
        left.updatedAt = 'left';
        const right = structuredClone(base);
        right.songs[0].title = 'A song changed';
        right.updatedAt = 'right';
        // Fire both saves concurrently and wait for both; this is the race the
        // lock must serialize without losing either side's edits. We intentionally
        // use `Promise.all` (not a serial pair) so a regression that lets writes
        // race past the lock would surface as a merge missing one of the two
        // fields.
        const results = await Promise.all([
          saveCatalogMerge(path, base, left),
          saveCatalogMerge(path, base, right)
        ]);
        expect(results).toHaveLength(2);
        const merged = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, 'utf8'));
        expect(merged.cooks[0].name).toBe('A changed');
        expect(merged.songs[0].title).toBe('A song changed');
      });
    
      test('orphan lock is reclaimed promptly (dead pid)', async () => {
        // Orphan reclaim: a batch killed mid-hold leaves the lock directory behind
        // with a dead owner pid. Siblings must reclaim immediately rather than
        // waiting out LOCK_STALE_MS and then blowing the acquire deadline.
        const lockPath = join(root, 'orphan.json.lock');
        const deadPid = deadPidForTest();
        mkdirSync(lockPath, { recursive: true });
        writeFileSync(join(lockPath, 'owner'), `${deadPid}\n`, 'utf8');
        const started = Date.now();
        await withFileLock(lockPath, async () => 'ok');
        const elapsed = Date.now() - started;
        expect(elapsed).toBeLessThan(5_000);
      });
    });
    
    /** A pid that is not running: probe upward from pid_max until kill(0) fails. */
    function deadPidForTest() {
      for (let pid = 4_194_303; pid > 1; pid--) {
        try {
          process.kill(pid, 0);
        } catch (error) {
          if (error?.code === 'ESRCH') return pid;
        }
      }
      throw new Error('could not find an unused pid for the orphan-lock test');
    }

        from pathlib import Path
        Path('docs/design/committer-stalls-2026-10-01.md').write_text('''# Committer stalls — 2026-10-01
        
        ## Cause and repair
        
        The classification spawn gate in dracon-sync 0.113.91 used
        `until.is_none_or(|until| now < *until)`. This admits jobs DURING a
        cooldown, removes the deadline, and blocks jobs AFTER expiry. It explains
        both dracon-strategy\'s 20,000+ rapid failures and the long quiet stalls.
        The corrected gate is `now >= *until`; the regression covers missing,
        future, exact, and expired deadlines.
        
        A targeted `sync-now` successfully committed and synced freeport (19 files),
        junk-runner (1), capture-anime-girls (39), doomtap (44), and dracon-platform
        (42). Strategy\'s existing commit was pushed fast-forward to github/gitlab.
        No history rewrites or worktree resets were used.
        
        Strategy\'s `ai-auto-music/catalog/cookbook.json` was 69,649,482 bytes;
        Warden\'s required clean filter refuses text over 67,108,864 bytes. Under
        the existing shared flock, the catalog was atomically compacted to
        53,784,216 bytes with parsed data equality verified. The shared JS JSON
        writer now compacts output when formatted JSON reaches 60 MiB. Its
        regression verifies a large formatted catalog fits and preserves all records.
        Other writers that do not use this helper can still reintroduce formatting;
        a catalog exceeding 64 MiB even when compact needs a separate storage design.
        
        ## Verification
        
        The recovered repos were reported synced by `repos --summary`. Active loops
        can introduce new edits immediately after each successful cycle.
        Full-workspace test/build/clippy attempts encountered a concurrent syntax
        error in dracon-system, so dracon-sync-only validation was run separately.
        Cargo deny passed. The catalog lock suite passed all three tests.
        
        Existing unrelated concerns include vanished monster-minecraft and the old
        nested folder-auto-banner path, and stale alternate remotes. These are not
        the cause of the recovered commit stalls; retiring or restoring them needs
        an operator decision about their intended locations/projects.
        ''')
        PY

        import subprocess,concurrent.futures
        paths=['/home/dracon/Dev/dracon-strategy','/home/dracon/Dev/dracon-platform']+['/home/dracon/Dev/dracon-platform/web/games/wip/'+n for n in ['junk-runner','capture-anime-girls','doomtap','freeport']]
        def check(p):
         head=subprocess.check_output(['git','-C',p,'rev-parse','HEAD'],text=True).strip()
         results=[]
         for remote in ['github','gitlab']:
          r=subprocess.run(['git','-C',p,'ls-remote',remote,'refs/heads/main'],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=25)
          sha=r.stdout.split()[0] if r.stdout.split() else 'unknown'
          results.append(remote+':'+('MATCH' if sha==head else sha[:12]))
         return p.split('/')[-1]+' '+head[:12]+' '+', '.join(results)
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=3) as ex:
         for result in ex.map(check,paths): print(result)
        PY

    /// Single `git log` call that extracts all commit metadata in one process.
    /// Returns (hash, author, relative_time, unix_timestamp, subject).
    /// Previously the report called this 3 times per repo (hash via libgit2,
    /// author via `%an`, time via `%ar`, timestamp via `%ct`) which tripled
    /// the wall-clock time on repos with many entries.
    pub(crate) async fn git_log_meta(repo: &Path) -> Option<(String, String, String, i64, String)> {
        let repo_str = repo.to_str()?;
        // %H = hash, %an = author, %ar = relative, %ct = unix, %s = subject
        // Separator `\x1f` (unit separator) is unlikely in commit fields.
        let out = crate::git::git_cmd()
            .args([
                "-C",
                repo_str,
                "log",
                "-1",
                "--format=%H%x1f%an%x1f%ar%x1f%ct%x1f%s",
            ])
            .output()
            .ok()?;
        if !out.status.success() {
            return None;
        }
        let line = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout);
        parse_git_log_meta_line(&line)
    }

    #!/usr/bin/env bun
    /**
     * Workstation-side synchronizer for the micro1-only Wave 11 renderer.
     *
     * This process never generates media. It pulls already-rendered files from
     * micro1, validates them, merges only the allowed catalog fields, mirrors the
     * files into the platform output tree, and acknowledges the remote files for
     * retirement. Every step is idempotent so a crash can be retried safely.
     */
    import {
      createHash,
    } from 'node:crypto';
    import {
      existsSync,
      mkdirSync,
      readFileSync,
      statSync,
      writeFileSync,
    } from 'node:fs';
    import { dirname, isAbsolute, relative, resolve } from 'node:path';
    import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
    import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
    
    const RSYNC_BIN = process.env.WAVE11_RSYNC_BIN ?? '/run/current-system/sw/bin/rsync';
    const PYTHON_BIN = process.env.WAVE11_PYTHON_BIN ?? '/etc/profiles/per-user/dracon/bin/python3';
    const FFPROBE_BIN = process.env.WAVE11_FFPROBE_BIN ?? '/etc/profiles/per-user/dracon/bin/ffprobe';
    import { atomicWriteJson, readJson, withFileLock } from './catalog-lock.mjs';
    
    const ROOT = resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');
    const REMOTE_HOST = process.env.WAVE11_REMOTE_HOST ?? 'micro1';

      .update(JSON.stringify(sanitizedCatalog, null, 2) + '\n')
      .digest('hex');

        'Generated by ai-auto-music/scripts/sync-to-platform.mjs from the canonical catalog. ' +
        'The SvelteKit app consumes this small manifest for catalog counts.',
      version: 1,
      updatedAt: new Date().toISOString(),

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    """Small per-cook inputs and atomic, field-scoped publication commits.
    
    The queue owns one cook at a time per slot. Files live in the canonical out/
    so interrupted render outputs can be reconciled by the existing generator.
    Only audio metadata is merged; unrelated recipes, covers and songs survive.
    """
    import argparse
    import json
    import os
    import re
    from pathlib import Path
    from catalog_flock import catalog_lock
    from audio_validation import validate_audio
    
    ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    AUDIO_FIELDS = ('audioKey', 'lengthSeconds', 'generationParams', 'createdAt')
    
    
    def atomic_json(path, value):
        temp = path.with_name(path.name + f'.tmp-{os.getpid()}')
        try:
            with temp.open('w') as f:
                json.dump(value, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
                f.write('\n')
                f.flush()
                os.fsync(f.fileno())
            os.replace(temp, path)
            fd = os.open(path.parent, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY)
            try:
                os.fsync(fd)
            finally:
                os.close(fd)
        finally:
            temp.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    
    
    WAVE_JOB_RE = re.compile(r'wave(9|10)-cook-\d+')
    WAVE_JOB_DIR = {9: '.wave9-jobs', 10: '.wave10-jobs'}
    
    
    def job_path(root, cook):
        m = WAVE_JOB_RE.fullmatch(cook)
        if not m:
            raise ValueError('invalid wave cook ID')
        wave_dir = WAVE_JOB_DIR.get(int(m.group(1)))
        if wave_dir is None:
            raise ValueError(f'unsupported wave: {m.group(1)}')
        return root / 'out' / wave_dir / cook / 'cookbook.json'
    
    
    def prepare(root, cook):
        path = job_path(root, cook)
        catalog = json.loads((root / 'catalog/cookbook.json').read_text())
        cooks = [c for c in catalog['cooks'] if c['id'] == cook]
        songs = [s for s in catalog['songs'] if s.get('cookId') == cook]
        if len(cooks) != 1 or len(songs) != 1:
            raise ValueError('expected one cook and one song')
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        # Keep completed private metadata after a crash before canonical commit.
        if path.exists():
            prior = json.loads(path.read_text())
            if [s['id'] for s in prior.get('songs', [])] != [songs[0]['id']]:
                raise ValueError('private job identity mismatch')
            if not songs[0].get('audioKey'):
                for field in AUDIO_FIELDS:
                    if field in prior['songs'][0]:
                        songs[0][field] = prior['songs'][0][field]
        atomic_json(path, {'version': 1, 'cooks': cooks, 'songs': songs})
        return path
    
    
    def commit(root, cook):
        path = job_path(root, cook)
        if not path.exists():
            raise ValueError(f'commit before prepare: {path}')
        job = json.loads(path.read_text())
        if len(job.get('songs', [])) != 1:
            raise ValueError('expected one result')
        result = job['songs'][0]
        if result.get('cookId') != cook:
            raise ValueError('cook mismatch')
        key = result.get('audioKey')
        if not isinstance(key, str):
            raise ValueError('render did not produce keyed audio')
        audio_root = (root / 'out/audio').resolve()
        audio = (root / 'out' / key).resolve()
        if not audio.is_relative_to(audio_root) or not audio.is_file() or audio.stat().st_size <= 1000:
            raise ValueError('invalid audio result')
        validate_audio(audio)
        catalog_path = root / 'catalog/cookbook.json'
        lock = catalog_path.with_name('cookbook.json.lock')
        with catalog_lock(lock):
            catalog = json.loads(catalog_path.read_text())
            matches = [s for s in catalog['songs'] if s['id'] == result['id'] and s.get('cookId') == cook]
            if len(matches) != 1:
                raise ValueError('canonical song identity mismatch')
            song = matches[0]
            if song.get('audioKey') and song['audioKey'] != key:
                raise ValueError('refusing to overwrite an already keyed song')
            for field in AUDIO_FIELDS:
                if field in result:
                    song[field] = result[field]
            from datetime import datetime, timezone
            catalog['updatedAt'] = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
            atomic_json(catalog_path, catalog)
        return key
    
    
    def main():
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        parser.add_argument('action', choices=('prepare', 'commit'))
        parser.add_argument('cook')
        args = parser.parse_args()
        print((prepare if args.action == 'prepare' else commit)(ROOT, args.cook), flush=True)
    
    
    if __name__ == '__main__':
        main()

        #[test]
        fn test_parse_git_log_meta_line_preserves_subject_with_separator() {
            // Commit subject that itself contains the unit-separator character

            // extra field.
            let line = "hash0\u{1f}author\u{1f}2 hours ago\u{1f}1700000000\u{1f}a\u{1f}b\u{1f}c";

    # Changelog
    
    All notable changes to `dracon-sync` will be documented in this file.
    
    The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
    and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
    
    > **Note**: prior to 0.112.12, `dracon-sync` was developed inside the
    > [`DraconDev/dracon-utilities`](https://github.com/DraconDev/dracon-utilities)
    > monorepo. Releases 0.0.0–0.112.11 are recorded in
    > [`dracon-utilities/CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/DraconDev/dracon-utilities/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
    > under the `dracon-sync` heading. From 0.112.12 onward, this CHANGELOG
    > is the canonical record.
    
    ## [Unreleased]
    ## [0.113.91] - 2026-09-28
    
    ### Fixed
    
    - **The committer was resource-starved by its own push-path pack-size
      guard, not by any repo being slow** (operator report 2026-09-28: "if you
      look at the commiter then its stuck"; `doomtap` dirty 14 h,
      `dracon-strategy` dirty 2 h). The proactive oversized-pack guard
      (`github_pack_too_large`, called from the push path on every push
      attempt) skips its cheap whole-`.git` fast path for any repo at or above
      the 2 GiB limit *by construction*, and `github_push_basis_bytes` then
      re-derived the object set per attempt. Two defects made that object set
      enormous:
      - **A duplicate-URL github remote poisoned the verdict.** The daemon
        configures a named `github` mirror alongside an `origin` pointing at the
        same repository (the fleet's SSH-mirror pattern), and the old code took
        the **max** across one scenario per remote name. A missing tracking ref
        on either is a FRESH-remote placeholder meaning "the whole branch
        ships", so one remote whose local ref happened to be absent forced a
        whole-history measurement even when its duplicate-URL sibling was valid
        and converged. Measured on the fleet: `darklord` 5.66 GiB and
        `endless-td` 4.62 GiB of objects measured to decide whether to push
        **0 bytes**. Scenarios are now deduped by canonical repository URL
        (`same_repository_url`'s `canonical_repository_url`), and within a
        duplicate-URL group the informed exclusion set wins over the
        fresh-remote placeholder — sound rather than merely cheaper, because
        two remotes with the same URL address the same remote, so an absent
        tracking ref on one is a gap in local bookkeeping, not a fact about the
        remote.
      - **A converged repo re-measured on every commit.** The verdict cache key
        contains the branch tip, so each new commit is a guaranteed miss, and
        the guard answered "nothing to push" by deriving the full object set. A
        converged repo is now recognised from the ref files alone (every github
        remote's tracking tip equals the branch tip) and short-circuits to
        `(false, 0)` with no `.git` walk, no `rev-list`, no `cat-file` and no
        `pack-objects`. The verdict is cached like any other, so cache
        population is unchanged.
    
      The cost of the old path, all measured on the fleet: two `git
      pack-objects --stdout` children running concurrently at 155% and 44% CPU
      and 1.14 GB / 184 MB RSS; the daemon's cgroup throttled in **441 of 451
      CPU periods (97.8%)** with 106 CPU-seconds of demand refused per 45 s
      wall, and pinned at `MemoryHigh`; classifications that take **1.19 s**
      (`ai-auto-writer`) and **4.97 s** (`monster-minecraft`) by hand timing out
      *inside* the daemon at 33 s and 36 s. Repos that lost the scheduler
      lottery sat dirty for hours.
    
      After the change, **0 repos** are forced into the multi-GiB
      `pack-objects` probe (was 2), and the daemon holds ~87% of one core with
      **0% throttled periods** and 0 CPU-seconds of refused demand.
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    # scripts/release.sh — cut a dracon-sync release end-to-end.
    #
    # This command releases the dracon-sync package from this repo: it updates
    # Cargo.toml/CHANGELOG/release notes, the standalone Cargo.lock, crates.io,
    # the dracon-sync-vX.Y.Z tag, and its GitHub release.
    #
    # Hard rules baked into this script:
    #   - The git tag is created only AFTER successful crates.io publish.
    #     The tag is the contract that "this version is on crates.io".
    #   - The repo working tree must be clean before starting. Run
    #     this through `dracon-sync maintenance -- ...` to avoid daemon races.
    #   - Every step is idempotent: re-running with the same version is a no-op
    #     or a clear "already done" message.
    #   - `--dry-run` runs every local validation step without mutating remote
    #     state (no real publish, push, tag, or GitHub release). It modifies the
    #     utility release surfaces and the workspace lockfile so the operator can
    #     inspect the diff; `--abort` reverts those changes.
    #
    # Usage:
    #   scripts/release.sh <version> [options]
    #
    #   <version>  e.g. 0.112.12  (NOT prefixed with 'v'; tag will be v<version>)
    #
    # Options:
    #   --dry-run             Run the pipeline end-to-end without mutating remote
    #                         state. Local release surfaces (utility Cargo.toml,
    #                         workspace Cargo.lock, CHANGELOG, release notes) ARE
    #                         modified so the operator can inspect the diff. Use
    #                         --abort to revert.
    #   --abort               Revert any local modifications made by --dry-run
    #                         (utility Cargo.toml + workspace lock + changelog +
    #                         release notes). Refuses to
    #                         run if the working tree contains pre-existing
    #                         modifications outside those release surfaces
    #                         (CORRECTED 2026-08-10, audit LOW: the guard is now
    #                         real — the abort path used to run unchecked).
    #   --remote <name>       Push to this git remote (default: auto-detect the
    #                         github.com remote via scripts/resolve-github-remote.sh).
    #   --yes                 Skip the interactive "are you sure" prompt before
    #                         push/publish/tag steps. Required for non-interactive
    #                         runs.
    #
    # Examples:
    #   scripts/release.sh 0.112.13 --dry-run        # safe preview
    #   scripts/release.sh 0.112.13 --yes            # real cut
    #   scripts/release.sh 0.112.13 --abort          # undo a dry-run
    #
    # Exit codes:
    #   0  success
    #   1  generic failure (inspect stdout/stderr)
    #   2  precondition violation (dirty tree, missing credentials, etc.)
    #   3  publish failed — tag NOT created, recovery steps in stderr
    
    set -euo pipefail
    
    # ----- paths ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # FIXED 2026-09-01 (post-monorepo conversion 2026-08-22): the previous
    # version of this script treated the utility directory as a standalone Git
    # repository. The utility directories are now tracked inside the parent
    # monorepo and are intentionally ignored for ordinary `git add`, so resolve
    # both roots explicitly and force-stage only the release paths below.
    SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    CRATE_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
    REPO_ROOT="$(git -C "$SCRIPT_DIR" rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
    CRATE_REL="${CRATE_DIR#"$REPO_ROOT"/}"
    # STANDALONE 2026-09-11 (nested-repo layout): the crate directory can
    # BE the git top-level now. Release surfaces are then repo-root-relative.
    if [[ "$CRATE_DIR" == "$REPO_ROOT" ]]; then CRATE_REL=""; fi
    # Repo-root-relative prefix for release surfaces ("" in standalone mode).
    RELPFX="${CRATE_REL:+$CRATE_REL/}"
    cd "$REPO_ROOT"
    
    CRATE_TOML="$CRATE_DIR/Cargo.toml"
    CHANGELOG="$CRATE_DIR/CHANGELOG.md"
    LOCKFILE="$REPO_ROOT/Cargo.lock"
    
    # ----- defaults ------------------------------------------------------------
    DRY_RUN=0
    ABORT=0
    REMOTE=""          # --remote override; empty = auto-detect the github.com remote
    ASSUME_YES=0
    VERSION=""
    CRATE_NAME="dracon-sync"
    
    # ----- argument parsing ----------------------------------------------------
    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
        case "$1" in
            --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
            --abort)   ABORT=1; shift ;;
            --remote)  REMOTE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --yes)     ASSUME_YES=1; shift ;;
            -h|--help)
                sed -n '2,40p' "$0"
                exit 0
                ;;
            -*)
                echo "❌ unknown flag: $1" >&2
                exit 1
                ;;
            *)
                if [[ -z "$VERSION" ]]; then
                    VERSION="$1"
                else
                    echo "❌ unexpected positional arg: $1" >&2
                    exit 1
                fi
                shift
                ;;
        esac
    done
    
    TAG="${CRATE_NAME}-v${VERSION}"
    TOTAL_STEPS=8
    
    # ----- colors (only on a tty) ---------------------------------------------
    if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
        C_RED=$'\033[31m'; C_GREEN=$'\033[32m'; C_YELLOW=$'\033[33m'
        # FIXED 2026-09-27 (audit rework round 3, F86): C_BOLD was assigned in
        # both branches and never read (shellcheck SC2034). Removed rather than
        # allow-listed so the colour set matches what the script actually uses.
        C_BLUE=$'\033[34m'; C_RESET=$'\033[0m'
    else
        C_RED=""; C_GREEN=""; C_YELLOW=""; C_BLUE=""; C_RESET=""
    fi
    
    # ----- helpers -------------------------------------------------------------
    log()    { printf '%s%s%s\n' "$C_BLUE" "$*" "$C_RESET"; }
    ok()     { printf '%s%s%s\n' "$C_GREEN" "✓ $*" "$C_RESET"; }
    warn()   { printf '%s%s%s\n' "$C_YELLOW" "⚠ $*" "$C_RESET"; }

    run_deny_gate() {

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    # scripts/verify-install.sh — post-install / pre-release fixture check for a
    # dracon-sync binary.
    #
    # Guards against the 2026-08-08 incident class: a binary built with an
    # unpatched dracon-git whose libgit2 status path counts gitignored files
    # (e.g. `.pi/`) as untracked, producing phantom untracked counts in
    # `dracon-sync repos` (endless-td 294, dracon-platform 48, ...) that can
    # never be committed. The trigger was `cargo publish` silently dropping the
    # workspace `[patch.crates-io]`, so `cargo install` resolved an old crates.io
    # dracon-git. The workspace build and the crates.io-resolved build must BOTH
    # report untracked=0 for a repo whose `.pi/` dir is gitignored — this script
    # asserts exactly that, behaviorally, against any binary you point it at.
    #
    # Usage:
    #   scripts/verify-install.sh [binary-path]
    #
    #   binary-path   default: `dracon-sync` (resolved via PATH) — i.e. the
    #                 installed binary the operator just put in place.
    #
    # Exit codes: 0 = fixture clean; 1 = fixture failed (gitignore handling
    # broken in the binary under test).
    set -euo pipefail
    
    BIN="${1:-dracon-sync}"
    if ! command -v "$BIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "✗ binary '$BIN' not found on PATH" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    
    TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
    trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
    
    # ── fixture repo: a single committed file + a gitignored `.pi/` dir ──────
    REPO="$TMP/repo"
    mkdir -p "$REPO/.pi"
    git -C "$REPO" init -q -b main
    git -C "$REPO" config user.email fixture@test.local
    git -C "$REPO" config user.name fixture
    git -C "$REPO" config core.hooksPath /dev/null
    echo "content" > "$REPO/f.txt"
    git -C "$REPO" add f.txt
    git -C "$REPO" commit -qm init
    printf '.pi/\n' > "$REPO/.gitignore"
    git -C "$REPO" add .gitignore
    git -C "$REPO" commit -qm ignore-rule
    for i in 1 2 3; do echo "x" > "$REPO/.pi/shot$i.png"; done
    
    # git CLI ground truth: 0 untracked (the ignore rule applies)
    if [[ "$(git -C "$REPO" ls-files --others --exclude-standard | wc -l)" != "0" ]]; then
        echo "✗ fixture self-check failed (git CLI sees untracked files)" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    
    cat > "$TMP/policy.toml" <<EOF
    watch_roots = ["$REPO"]
    EOF
    
    # ── run the binary under test and read its untracked count ───────────────
    # DRACON_SYNC_POLICY wires the fixture policy into the binary under test so
    # `repos --json` scans ONLY the fixture repo. (FIXED 2026-08-09, audit HIGH:
    # the env was previously unset, so the check asserted rows[0] of the
    # operator's REAL fleet — passing only while the fleet happens to be clean
    # and false-failing whenever a legitimately-dirty fleet repo is row 0.)
    OUT="$(DRACON_SYNC_POLICY="$TMP/policy.toml" "$BIN" repos --json 2>/dev/null || true)"
    UNTRACKED="$(printf '%s' "$OUT" | python3 -c '
    import json, sys
    try:
        d = json.load(sys.stdin)
        rows = d["rows"] if isinstance(d, dict) and "rows" in d else d
        print(rows[0]["untracked"] if rows else "-1")
    except Exception:
        print("-1")
    ' 2>/dev/null || echo "-1")"
    SCANNED="$(printf '%s' "$OUT" | python3 -c '
    import json, sys
    try:
        d = json.load(sys.stdin)
        rows = d["rows"] if isinstance(d, dict) and "rows" in d else d
        print(rows[0]["repo"] if rows else "")
    except Exception:
        print("")
    ' 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
    
    if [[ "$SCANNED" != "$REPO" ]]; then
        echo "✗ FAIL: '$BIN' scanned '$SCANNED' — expected the fixture repo '$REPO'." >&2
        echo "  The fixture policy (\$DRACON_SYNC_POLICY=$TMP/policy.toml) was not honored; the" >&2
        echo "  check would silently test the operator's real fleet instead of the fixture." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    
    if [[ "$UNTRACKED" != "0" ]]; then
        echo "✗ FAIL: '$BIN' reports untracked=$UNTRACKED for a repo whose only untracked files are gitignored (.pi/)." >&2
        echo "  Expected 0. This is the 2026-08-08 phantom-untracked incident: the binary was" >&2
        echo "  built against an unpatched dracon-git whose libgit2 status path ignores rules" >&2
        echo "  differently from git CLI. See docs/design/installed-binary-drops-patch-dracon-git-2026-08-08.md." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    echo "✓ OK: '$BIN' reports untracked=0 — gitignore handling intact."

    die()    { printf '%s%s%s\n' "$C_RED" "✗ $*" "$C_RESET" >&2; exit 1; }
    die_pre(){ printf '%s%s%s\n' "$C_RED" "✗ $*" "$C_RESET" >&2; exit 2; }
    die_pub(){ printf '%s%s%s\n' "$C_RED" "✗ $*" "$C_RESET" >&2; exit 3; }
    
    run() {
        # Print the command, then run it. Honors DRY_RUN.
        printf '   $ %s\n' "$*"
        if [[ $DRY_RUN -eq 1 ]]; then
            printf '   (skipped: --dry-run)\n'
            return 0
        fi
        "$@"
    }
    
    run_local() {
        # Commands using this helper are local validation steps. They are safe
        # during --dry-run and must still execute so a preview exercises the
        # package and dependency-resolution checks it claims to run.
        printf '   $ %s\n' "$*"
        "$@"
    }
    
    require_clean_tree() {
        if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || \
           [[ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]] || \
           [[ -n "$(release_note_files)" ]]; then
            die_pre "working tree is dirty; commit or stash before releasing"
        fi
    }
    
    require_cmd() {
        command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die_pre "missing required command: $1"
    }
    
    require_credentials() {
        require_cmd gh; require_cmd cargo
        gh auth status >/dev/null 2>&1 \
            || die_pre "gh not authenticated; run 'gh auth login' first"
        [[ -f "$HOME/.cargo/credentials.toml" ]] \
            || die_pre "missing ~/.cargo/credentials.toml; run 'cargo login <token>' first"
    }
    
    is_release_surface() {
        local path=$1
        [[ "$path" == "${RELPFX}Cargo.toml" ||
           "$path" == "${RELPFX}CHANGELOG.md" ||
           "$path" == "Cargo.lock" ||
           "$path" == "${RELPFX}"release-notes-v*.md ]]
    }
    
    release_note_files() {
        # The parent .gitignore intentionally ignores the utility directory, so
        # include ignored-but-untracked release notes when handling --abort.
        git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard -- \
            "${RELPFX}release-notes-v*.md" 2>/dev/null || true
    }
    
    confirm_remote_mutation() {
        [[ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 || "$ASSUME_YES" -eq 1 ]] && return 0
        if [[ ! -t 0 ]]; then
            die_pre "--yes is required for a non-interactive real release"
        fi
        local answer
        if ! read -r -p "Publish ${CRATE_NAME}@${VERSION}, tag ${TAG}, and push to ${REMOTE}? [y/N] " answer; then
            die_pre "release confirmation was not provided"
        fi
        case "${answer,,}" in
            y|yes) ;;
            *) die_pre "release cancelled" ;;
        esac
    }

        # the affected local package entry here; unlike generate-lockfile this
        # does not discard the monorepo's intentionally pinned dependency graph.

    # Dracon Sync
    
    **Invisible git sync for development.** An auto-commit, multi-mirror daemon that watches your repos, commits every change with deterministic, facts-based messages, and pushes to GitHub, GitLab, and Codeberg simultaneously.
    
    ![`dracon-sync repos` output](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DraconDev/dracon-sync-background-auto-commit-multi-remote/main/docs/status-output.png)
    
    This page is the user guide for `dracon-sync` (also rendered on
    crates.io). This repo is the canonical, live source on `main`
    (mirrored to GitLab and Codeberg). For workspace builds it is also
    checked out as a nested standalone repo under `dracon-sync/` in the
    [`dracon-utilities`](https://github.com/DraconDev/dracon-utilities)
    parent repo — a regular nested repo, not a submodule.
    
    ## Install
    
    ```bash
    cargo install dracon-sync
    ```
    
    The binary lands at `~/.cargo/bin/dracon-sync` (version 0.113.55 on
    crates.io). The shipped systemd unit runs `%h/.local/bin/dracon-sync`, so
    for service use either copy it there or install from a checkout:

    Cargo.lock

    for service use either copy it there or install from a checkout:
    
    ```bash
    # Clone the repo

    ```
    
    Or, from a full `dracon-utilities` checkout, run `./install.sh` at the
    parent root to install all three utilities plus services and hooks in
    one pass.
    
    ## Why This Exists
    
    Other tools solve parts of the problem:
    - **git-auto-sync**: Auto-commits a single repo, no mirroring
    - **gitea-mirror**: One-way mirror to a single Forgejo instance, no auto-commit
    - **git-bridge**: Multi-provider sync, but no auto-commit or AI
    - **swarf**: Invisible sync for AI agents, but only a side-band directory
    
    **dracon-sync** is the only tool that combines all of these into one daemon:
    
    | Capability | git-auto-sync | gitea-mirror | git-bridge | swarf | **dracon-sync** |
    |---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
    | Auto-commit on change | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
    | Multi-repo watch | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ |
    | Multi-provider mirror | ❌ | ✅ (→1) | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ (3+) |
    | Deterministic commit messages | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
    | Version bump + release | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
    | Safety guards | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
    | Visibility sync | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
    | Broken tracking repair | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |

    # Sanctioned slimming — operator history rewrites for size (2026-09-26)
    
    ## Why this exists
    
    Under commit-all + never-rewrite, reachable history is monotonically
    non-decreasing: deleting a huge file from the worktree stops new growth
    but leaves every committed byte counting against the 2 GiB guard
    forever. Worktree deletion without history rewrite is not a size fix.
    The 2026-07-25 no-rewrite rule was written about *coordination* (loops
    racing the daemon's seconds-fast pushes), not size — this document adds
    the missing third path: operator-executed, fully coordinated slimming.
    
    ## What it is not
    
    - Loops/agents working in watched repos MUST still never rewrite
      history (see AGENTS.md "Agent loops MUST NOT rewrite history").
      They cannot coordinate, hold a pause, or verify a cutover.
    - It is not a substitute for bucket-overflow: slimming fixes the
      past, overflow keeps bulky regenerable content out of history in
      the future. The `*.sqlite`/`*.db` class (auto-committed up to
      100 MB by policy) is overflow's first bite point.
    
    ## When it applies
    
    A repo breaches (or is trending into) the 2 GiB bucket-guard policy
    estimate AND the bloat is an excisable class (regenerable dumps,
    superseded media, loop scratch) — never shipped product assets,
    unless the operator explicitly reclassifies them.
    
    ## Procedure (all steps, in order)
    
    1. **Bundle backup**: `git bundle create
       ~/dracon/backups/<repo>-pre-slim-YYYYMMDD.bundle --all`, then
       `git bundle verify`. No rewrite without a verified bundle.
    2. **Scratch rewrite**: clone to `~/dracon/conv-work/<repo>`
       (outside daemon watch roots), run
       `git filter-repo --invert-paths --path <class>... --force`.
       Dry-run first on unfamiliar specs.
    3. **Guard-verify the rewritten history**: run
       `web/scripts/bucket-strategy-guard.sh` against the scratch tip.
       Policy estimate must read under 2 GiB or stop here.
    4. **Cutover in one maintenance window**:
       `dracon-sync maintenance --` push the rewritten tip with
       `--force-with-lease=<old>:<new>` to github, gitlab, and origin
       in the same window. Preconditions: GitLab `main` unprotected
    ✓ • 0ms

    # Repository bucket strategy
    
    **Status:** active policy, offline and forward-only. This document is the operator runbook for the shared `dracon-master` bucket strategy. It does not authorize live bucket mutations.
    
    ## Policy in one minute
    
    - One physical bucket: `dracon-master` at the OVH endpoint `https://s3.uk.io.cloud.ovh.net/`.
    - Namespaces are part of the object key, not a second bucket: `platform/dracon-platform`, `games/<game>`, `music`, `books`, and `studio`.
    - The tracked policy is [`web/config/bucket-strategy.json`](../config/bucket-strategy.json). The tracked migration inventory is [`bucket-migration-inventory.json`](bucket-migration-inventory.json).
    - Existing binaries are **not** automatically eligible. A repository opts in with a manifest containing only public, browser-consumable, explicitly regenerable entries. The inventory classifier remains broader than the promotion allowlist so opaque blobs are still surfaced when unlisted.
    - Development is cache-first: a valid local cache file wins; a cache miss uses the configured development CDN route. Production uses the direct public URL.
    - The planner is deterministic and offline: `node web/scripts/bucket-strategy.mjs plan --repo <repo> --json`. It reads files and Git metadata only; it does not upload, delete, list, or mutate OVH.
    - The high-water guard measures the complete local reachable object graph for the repository's actual push remotes (including tags and other local refs) and compares the measured stored-pack size — plus a 5% re-pack reserve — against the operator policy limit. Unknown providers, missing remotes, missing limits, and measurement failures fail closed.
    
    ## Object-key layout
    
    Use a stable repository/game namespace and content-addressed generated objects:
    
    ```text
    games/hegemon/<logical-path>/<sha256>.<ext>
    platform/dracon-platform/<logical-path>/<sha256>.<ext>
    music/<logical-path>/<sha256>.<ext>
    ```
    
    The namespace is selected by the repository inventory record. Never use a private source path, credential, access key, or secret as a logical path or object key. Manifest visibility is always `public`; source code and credentials are not promotion candidates.
    
    ## Manifest contract
    
    A repository manifest is a tracked JSON file. The current schema is:
    
    ```json
    {
      "schemaVersion": 1,
      "bucket": "dracon-master",
      "repository": "games/example",
      "namespace": "games/example",
      "assets": [
        {
          "id": "brand-logo",
          "kind": "image",
          "sourcePath": "assets/generated/brand-logo.png",
          "logicalPath": "brand/logo.png",
          "objectKey": "games/example/brand/{sha256}.{ext}",
          "sha256": "<64 lowercase hex characters>",
          "bytes": 1234,
          "regenerable": true,
          "visibility": "public",
          "generator": {
            "command": "bun run generate:brand",
            "inputs": ["assets/source/brand.svg"]
          }
        }
      ]
    }
    ```
    
    Every entry must be explicit and satisfy all of these rules:
    
    1. `regenerable` is exactly `true` and `visibility` is exactly `public`.
    2. `sourcePath` and `logicalPath` are safe repository-relative slash paths, and their extensions match case-insensitively. This keeps the planner and runtime resolver's `{ext}` materialization on the same object key; a format conversion must produce a new source file rather than relabeling bytes.
    3. `objectKey` is inside the manifest namespace and is safe for S3.
    4. `sha256` and `bytes` match the current source file.
    5. `generator.command` explains how the source is reproduced.
    6. The source extension is in the browser-consumable promotion allowlist (images, audio/video, fonts, PDF, glTF/GLB, or WebAssembly). Opaque archives, model runtimes, and `.bin`/`.onnx` blobs may still be classified as unlisted inventory assets, but cannot be promoted by this manifest.
    7. IDs, logical paths, and object-key templates are unique.
    
    A manifest with no assets is a valid **empty** opt-in/index. The current platform manifest is intentionally empty. The shared games manifest contains one explicit, source-backed regenerable brand favicon and is consumed by the games shell; it does not classify any other existing binary as regenerable.
    
    Legacy resolver manifests remain supported: a `Record<string, string>` mapping and existing `~bucket-asset/<slug>/<logical-path>` imports continue to work. Structured keyed maps and document manifests (`assets` or `entries`) are also accepted by the resolver.
    
    ## Offline promotion workflow
    
    From the platform root:
    
    ```sh
    # Validate policy, inventory, manifests, and eligible-root declarations.
    node web/scripts/bucket-strategy.mjs check --repo . --json
    
    # Produce a sorted, content-addressed plan. This is a dry run only.
    node web/scripts/bucket-strategy.mjs plan --repo . --json
    
    # Optional: inspect a fixture or nested checkout explicitly.
    node web/scripts/bucket-strategy.mjs plan \
      --repo web/games/wip/example --manifest web/config/bucket-manifests/example.json --json
    ```
    
    The plan includes the repository namespace, logical path, source path, SHA-256, byte count, resolved object key, and public URL for every declared entry. `liveOperations` is always `false`. The same inputs produce the same `planId`; the command does not alter source files, the index, refs, or the bucket.
    
    The plan is intentionally separate from publishing. A future operator-approved publisher may consume a reviewed plan, but this strategy does not contain an upload/delete path and must not be wired to the live OVH scripts without a separate review.
    
    ## Migration classification and inventory
    
    [`web/docs/bucket-migration-inventory.json`](bucket-migration-inventory.json) is the migration ledger. Each repository is one of:
    
    - `legacy`: existing tracked content is grandfathered and not eligible by implication.
    - `pilot`: a deliberately limited experiment; it still needs a manifest before promotion.
    - `declared`: a repository has opted into the manifest contract.
    - `empty`: an explicitly empty manifest/index; it contains no promoted assets.
    
    `legacyRoots`, `temporaryRoots`, and `intentionalRoots` document exclusions. `eligibleRoots` are the only roots from which an unlisted asset is treated as a policy error. The check command reports unclassified eligible assets and fails; it never silently promotes or deletes them.
    
    Migration is forward-only:
    
    1. Add a tracked manifest describing only a genuinely regenerable public asset.
    2. Generate/review the source and run the offline plan.
    3. Move future consumers to the logical manifest path.
    4. Keep old Git objects and existing tracked files as legacy history/content; do not rewrite history or untrack them as part of this strategy.
    5. The pre-commit and pre-push guards reject deletion, `git rm --cached`, and rename-away of protected tracked inventory roots or manifest source paths. Keep the prior file and fix the consumer or manifest instead of removing the source.
    6. If a plan or publication fails, stop and retain the previous manifest and public URLs. Do not delete the old object as an automatic rollback step.
    
    ## Resolution behavior
    
    The shared package [`web/packages/ovh-bucket`](../packages/ovh-bucket/) exposes `normalizeAssetManifest`, `resolveAssetUrl`, and `bulkResolve`:
    
    - In development, a real file under the configured cache root resolves to `/@bucket-cache/<object-key>`.
    - A cache miss resolves to the development CDN prefix (normally `/_game-cdn/<object-key>`), allowing the existing Caddy fallback to fetch the public object.
    - In production, it returns the direct HTTPS public URL.
    - Missing entries, unsafe paths/keys, source/logical extension mismatches, insecure URLs, and cache symlink escapes fail closed.
    - The Vite plugin reads only an in-memory manifest or a local `manifestPath`; it never fetches a manifest, reads credentials, or contacts OVH.
    
    The games Vite app uses the checked-in shared index at `web/config/bucket-manifests/games.json` and actively imports `~bucket-asset/games/brand/favicon.png` in `src/routes/+layout.svelte`. Individual game repositories can provide their own local manifest when they explicitly declare assets. The music Vite integration remains unchanged because its existing configuration documents a SvelteKit/plugin compatibility issue; the shared resolver remains available to it without forcing that plugin.
    
    ## Provider high-water guard
    
    The policy currently configures:
    
    | Provider | Limit | Source |
    |---|---:|---|
    | GitHub | 5,905,580,032 bytes (5.5 GiB) | operator policy for this repository's measured pack |
    | GitLab | 5,905,580,032 bytes (5.5 GiB) | same measured-pack operator policy as GitHub |
    
    Both providers carry the same number on purpose. The limit is **not** a published
    provider cap: it is this repository's own budget, and the evidence for it is a
    measurement of this repository taken on 2026-09-27 — `git count-objects -vH`
    reported `size-pack: 4.30 GiB`, and the guard's `storedBytes` over the pushable set
    was 4,491,076,996 bytes (4.18 GiB). 5.5 GiB is that measured pack plus a ~28% growth
    budget, so the guard trips about 1.2 GiB of growth from here. Before 2026-09-27 the
    policy carried 2.00 GiB (GitHub) and 4.88 GiB (GitLab) as if they were provider
    facts, and the guard then failed closed on *every* commit — which is what forced
    `--no-verify`, silently disabling the warden `.env` secret check and the
    audit-ledger append-only clause in the same hook.
    
    The guard resolves actual push URLs, recognizes GitHub and GitLab SCP/URL forms, and selects the **lowest** applicable configured limit. It does not infer a limit for an unconfigured provider such as Codeberg. If a configured push remote is unknown, the guard refuses to guess. If a repository has no push remote, it also fails closed.
    
    Sizing uses the complete reachable object set (`git rev-list --objects --all` plus every requested push ref) and strict `git cat-file --batch-check` metadata. The measurement validates every object record, closes recursively over packed delta bases (including bases reached through alternates), and records the local stored-object sum. A thin pack whose external base is not locally measurable fails closed. Because a hook must not spend minutes repacking a multi-gigabyte repository, it does **not** run `git pack-objects`.
    
    **The guard gates on the stored pack, not on the uncompressed object sum** (2026-09-27). Git stores every object zlib-compressed and delta-compressed, so raw object bytes are several times the pack a provider actually holds — measured on this repository: 26,040,290,218 raw bytes (24.25 GiB) against a 4.30 GiB pack. Comparing the raw sum with a provider-sized limit therefore failed closed on every commit. The gate is now:
    
    ```text
    storedBytes + ceil(storedBytes * 5%) + prospectiveCommitAllowanceBytes
    ```
    
    The 5% re-pack reserve is the observed pack-versus-stored gap on this repository
    (4.30 / 4.18 = 2.9%) rounded up. With it, the measured basis is 4.39 GiB against the
    5.5 GiB policy budget.
    
    The raw-based estimate is still computed and reported, but only as a diagnostic:
    
    ```text
    rawBytes + ceil(rawBytes * 10%) + 128 * objectCount + 65,536
    ```
    
    It is **not** the gate, and it is not a mathematical upper bound on every pack a
    provider could theoretically emit. The complete graph, all local refs, alternates,
    and packed delta-base closure prevent known local undercounts; the pre-push hook
    remains the authoritative final gate after the actual commit exists.
    
    A staged pre-commit measurement builds an isolated temporary index and object database, includes the prospective tree, and removes the temporary context without mutating the real index or object database. It adds a fixed 65,536-byte prospective-commit allowance plus the size of a regular `COMMIT_EDITMSG` file when one is available. That fixed reserve is a policy cushion, not a proof for arbitrary commit messages, signatures, or metadata; ordinary `git commit -m` does not reliably expose its final message to the pre-commit hook. Pre-push measures the actual post-commit graph, so a pathological prospective commit is still blocked at the final boundary. Repository-discovery, temporary object-database, namespace, graft, replacement, and shallow-boundary environment overrides are rejected; linked worktrees and repository-managed alternates are supported. A legitimate `GIT_INDEX_FILE` is preserved for staged measurement and copied into an isolated temporary index. `info/grafts` must be absent, an empty regular file, or a non-empty regular file is rejected; directories, symlinks, FIFOs, and other special files are rejected before any read can block. Git subprocesses set `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, so promisor repositories fail closed rather than contacting a remote while being sized.
    
    Run it manually with:
    
    ```sh
    node web/scripts/bucket-strategy.mjs guard --repo . --json
    node web/scripts/bucket-strategy.mjs guard --repo . --staged --json
    ```
    
    The JSON result labels the basis as `complete-reachable-stored-pack-plus-repack-reserve` and includes `uncompressedBytes`, `storedBytes`, `storedPackBytes`, `storedPackReserveBytes`, `storedPackReservePercent`, `pushableBytes`, `objectCount`, `deltaBaseCount`, `policyEstimateBytes`, `packPolicyEstimateBytes`, and `prospectiveCommitAllowanceBytes` for auditability. `projectedBytes` and `maxBasisBytes` are the stored-pack basis — the number the limit is compared against. `policyEstimateBytes` is the retired raw-based estimate, retained as a diagnostic only. The older `packUpperBoundBytes` field remains as a compatibility alias for that raw-based diagnostic, but its historical name does not turn it into a formal upper-bound proof, and it is not the gate. `--no-size` remains a forward-only diagnostic and is never a push approval.
    
    The parent platform has active tracked [`.githooks/pre-commit`](../.githooks/pre-commit) and [`.githooks/pre-push`](../.githooks/pre-push). They run the local offline guard and then chain the machine-global Warden hooks, preserving secret, audit-ledger, and history protections. `web/scripts/install-git-hooks.sh` keeps the active hook path and tracked hook copies synchronized.
    
    ### Nested repositories
    
    Nested game repositories use one of two durable hook layouts. Repositories with custom local policy keep tracked `.githooks` wrappers generated from [`web/scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit-shared.sh`](../scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit-shared.sh) and [`pre-push-shared.sh`](../scripts/git-hooks/pre-push-shared.sh); an existing hook is preserved as `pre-*.dracon-original`. Repositories without custom local hooks use the checked-in shared dispatch directory [`bucket-hooks`](../scripts/git-hooks/bucket-hooks/) through a checkout-relative `core.hooksPath`, so cleanup of an active nested worktree cannot remove the installation. Both layouts chain the machine-global Warden hook, and both pass the nested checkout's actual remotes to the offline guard. The installer [`install-nested-bucket-hooks.sh`](../scripts/git-hooks/install-nested-bucket-hooks.sh) discovers direct game repositories, upgrades old canonical wrappers without recursively chaining them, preserves custom hooks, refuses symlinked or conflicting hook sources, and stops a partial rollout if one hook cannot be installed safely. For custom-hook repositories it installs both wrappers before changing `core.hooksPath`, so a failed second-hook preservation leaves the previous effective policy in place. Shared dispatch never executes preserved files that happen to live beside the platform source wrapper. Use `--check` to verify the rollout without writing. No parent hook is copied over unrelated worktree policy.
    
    **The 5.5 GiB budget is shared.** `loadPolicy()` resolves the nearest ancestor holding a `web/config/bucket-strategy.json`, and no game repository carries one today, so every nested game repository is measured against the parent policy. That means the 2026-09-27 re-basing also moved their high-water limit from 2.00 GiB to 5.5 GiB — a looser tripwire for a size class that does not need it (the measured `web/games/wip/neonbreak` pushable size is 1.21 GiB). A repository that needs its own budget should add a `web/config/bucket-strategy.json` at its own root with its own `providerLimits`; nearest-ancestor resolution picks it up with no code change. This is recorded rather than silently absorbed, because widening the parent limit is what widened theirs.
    
    ## Recovery and safety rules
    
    - **No live operations:** do not run OVH list/upload/delete/policy commands as part of planning or validation. Never read `web/.env.ovh` for this strategy.
    - **No history surgery:** do not amend, rebase, filter, force-push, untrack existing assets, or delete legacy data.
    - **Fail closed:** malformed policy/manifests, unknown remotes/providers, missing limits, missing source hashes, unclassified eligible assets, and unmeasurable Git state are errors.
    - **Secrets:** public asset URLs and source paths are not an authorization channel. Keep credentials, private source, tokens, keys, and age files out of manifests and bucket keys.
    - **Rollback:** retain the prior manifest/URL mapping and stop promotion. Recover by correcting the manifest or generator and producing a new reviewed plan; never perform an automatic destructive bucket rollback.
    - **Daemon safety:** the daemon may commit and push automatically. If an operator must perform Git surgery, use `dracon-sync maintenance -- <command>`; do not manually stop the daemon.
    
    ## Evidence and tests
    
    Focused offline tests:
    
    ```sh
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    # Portable, offline repository-size guard for platform Git hooks.
    #
    # This wrapper is safe to call from a parent or nested checkout. It forwards
    # only explicit arguments to the local strategy CLI, locates the platform
    # script from the checkout ancestry, and fails closed when the platform
    # strategy cannot be found. It never contacts OVH, GitHub, or GitLab.
    set -euo pipefail
    
    SCRIPT_DIR="$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    REPO_ROOT="${DRACON_BUCKET_REPO_ROOT-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)}"

      set -- --staged --json

        "${DRACON_BUCKET_STRATEGY-}" \
        "$SCRIPT_DIR/bucket-strategy.mjs" \
        "$REPO_ROOT/web/scripts/bucket-strategy.mjs"; do
        if [ -n "$candidate" ] && [ -f "$candidate" ]; then
          printf '%s\n' "$candidate"
          return 0
        fi
      done
      local current="$REPO_ROOT"
      while [ "$current" != "/" ]; do
        candidate="$current/web/scripts/bucket-strategy.mjs"
        if [ -f "$candidate" ]; then
          printf '%s\n' "$candidate"
          return 0
        fi
        current="$(dirname -- "$current")"
      done
      candidate="/web/scripts/bucket-strategy.mjs"
      if [ -f "$candidate" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$candidate"
        return 0
      fi
      return 1

    STRATEGY_SCRIPT="$(find_strategy || true)"
    if [ -z "$STRATEGY_SCRIPT" ]; then
      echo "bucket-strategy: cannot locate bucket-strategy.mjs; refusing to guess" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "bucket-strategy: node is required for the offline size guard" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    
    exec node "$STRATEGY_SCRIPT" guard --repo "$REPO_ROOT" "$@"

## Assistant

**Currently, exceeding a cap does not automatically move files to the bucket.** The committer blocks or skips the affected operation.

| Limit | Current behavior |
|---|---|
| File exceeds 100 MiB | Daemon leaves it unstaged. |
| GitHub push exceeds 2 GiB | Daemon skips that GitHub push; other remotes may continue. |
| Platform/game repository exceeds its configured budget—currently 5.5 GiB | Installed bucket guards reject the commit or push. |

The table’s **SIZE is local Git storage**, while GitHub’s 2 GiB limit applies to **one push**. A repo larger than 2 GiB can therefore keep syncing small updates. [GitHub documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/using-git/troubleshooting-the-2-gb-push-limit)

Your bucket tooling has an explicit planning/publishing workflow, but it isn’t connected to the daemon as automatic overflow. The reviewed publisher currently supports the music namespace. [Bucket publisher](/home/dracon/Dev/dracon-platform/web/scripts/bucket-promote.mjs:1)

Automatic overflow would need to happen **before bulky files enter Git**: select declared assets, upload and verify them, then commit their manifest references. Source code and private data need separate handling.

Moving files to the bucket later **doesn’t remove their existing Git history**. That accumulated size requires the documented slimming procedure.

So everything is syncing now, but **automatic bucket overflow remains an implementation gap**.

## Assistant

I suggest **automatic bucket storage for approved bulky assets before they enter Git**, starting with music, where the publisher already exists.

- **Keep source, tests, docs, and configuration in Git.** Declare which generated media can use the bucket; don’t infer eligibility from size alone.
- **Upload → verify → commit a manifest reference.** Keep a local cache so development works normally and files can be restored by hash.
- **Fail visibly if uploading fails.** Preserve the local file and report “bucket upload pending”; never silently omit it or claim the repo is synced.
- **Warn before caps are reached.** Track repository growth and the next push’s size separately.
- **Handle existing bloat separately.** Bucket storage prevents future growth; backed-up, operator-approved slimming removes accumulated history.

I’d pilot this on a small set of declared music assets, verify upload failures and recovery, then extend it to generated game and book media. **I wouldn’t automatically move arbitrary files just because a repository crosses a cap.**

## Assistant

**Submodules were a sensible choice for organizing independent projects. They are insufficient as the long-term storage strategy.** We also had implementation problems, but fixing those doesn’t remove the underlying growth problem.

A submodule gives each game its own history and lets the platform reference one commit. That reduces the parent’s scope and allows independent development. Each game’s history can still grow indefinitely, though. Splitting a large repository into smaller repositories distributes that growth. [Git’s submodule documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitsubmodules)

Your own audit shows why this matters: it attributed **15.9 GB of historical blob content** to repeated versions of the music catalog, whose working copy was about 38 MB. Repository boundaries alone cannot solve that pattern. [Bloat analysis](/home/dracon/Dev/dracon-utilities/docs/design/parent-bloat-quarantine-analysis-2026-09-26.md:1)

I think the missing piece is a clear agreement about **where each kind of data lives and how we recover it**:

| Content | Sensible home |
|---|---|
| Source, tests, configuration, authored documents | Git |
| Large media and versioned datasets | Object storage, with version references in Git |
| Derived catalogs and build outputs | Rebuild from canonical inputs; preserve valuable snapshots separately |
| Logs, sessions, databases, audit recordings | Archive or snapshot storage with an explicit retention policy |
| Sensitive content | Warden-controlled encryption and access rules, whichever storage holds it |

This preserves your principle that nothing valuable should be left out. Git can record the exact version and location of a large payload without containing every payload byte.

I would keep **Warden responsible for security** and **Sync responsible for durability**. Sync should coordinate storage placement, upload verification, manifest commits, and restoration. Warden should decide which bytes require encryption and what may be public. We should avoid introducing a second independent uploader that races Sync over the same files.

That distinction matters because your current bucket workflow supports declared **public assets**. A complete preservation system also needs private or encrypted archives. Automatically routing an oversized file through the existing public-media workflow would be the wrong default.

For a bucket-backed file, a successful sync should mean:

1. Its exact payload has been uploaded and verified.
2. Git records the immutable object reference and integrity information.
3. A fresh checkout can restore that version.
4. Historical references remain recoverable under the chosen backup and retention policy.

The bucket then becomes part of the repository’s recovery requirements. A green Git push alone would no longer prove everything is backed up.

I’d retain the current project boundaries, introduce this storage contract gradually, and start with music because its publishing machinery already exists. I’d also break the growing catalog into stable records or shards—or generate it from smaller canonical inputs—so one changed song doesn’t require processing a 60–70 MB document.

Existing accumulated history needs a separate, backed-up cleanup. Future storage placement won’t reclaim those old Git objects.

**My assessment is that the submodule strategy was useful, and some execution was faulty, but the larger design remained incomplete: automatic preservation was implemented mainly as automatic Git commits. We need automatic preservation across Git and object storage, with one coordinated security and recovery contract.**

**Yes, I think a hybrid is the way forward—but small, stable videos can still belong in Git.** We need a predictable rule based on the file’s purpose, size, and how often it changes.

First, the **2 GiB limit is per GitHub push**, rather than a total repository cap. A larger repo can continue receiving small updates. [GitHub documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/using-git/troubleshooting-the-2-gb-push-limit)

“Put videos in Git while the repo is under 2 GiB” would therefore be a fragile rule. A 25 MB video regenerated 100 times represents roughly 2.5 GB of versions before Git’s compression and delta savings. Its current size hides its historical cost.

I’d use this policy:

| Situation | Default |
|---|---|
| Small, final media that changes rarely | Git is fine |
| Render previews, intermediate videos, frequently regenerated assets | Local cache plus external preservation where required |
| Large final media, including irreplaceable work | Versioned bucket storage, with references in Git |
| Source files and generation inputs | Git |

For a concrete starting point, **20 MiB could be the default threshold for media**, with documented exceptions. That’s our own practical threshold, not a provider limit. Frequently regenerated media would use external storage even below it; a deliberately retained, stable clip could have an exception.

The important part is that **placement stays consistent**. A clip shouldn’t unexpectedly switch storage because an unrelated part of the repo grew. Repository growth should produce early warnings and a review of what’s accumulating. It shouldn’t automatically relocate arbitrary files or rewrite history.

For your platform and games, I would:

- Keep the existing project boundaries and submodules.
- Keep small, stable shipped assets in Git.
- Route rendering intermediates and large media outside Git from creation.
- Preserve exact external versions so old commits remain reproducible.

The remaining decision is retention: whether every temporary render must remain recoverable forever, or whether some can expire. Putting them in a bucket changes where growth happens; retention determines whether that growth remains bounded.

That gives us a usable rule without banning videos from Git or pretending that today’s repo size predicts tomorrow’s history.

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    """git clean filter: stdin=file bytes, argv[1]=repo-relative path.
    
    - Pointer input -> pass through (idempotent; promotion output re-adds cleanly).
    - Non-allowlisted ext or over cap -> pass bytes through unchanged + warn.
    - Else upload to quarantine/ (content-addressed, idempotent), update the
      manifest on disk (unstaged; the commit-all daemon picks it up next cycle),
      emit pointer bytes to stdout.
    - Offline / no write key -> pass bytes through + warn (L3 spill catches it later).
    Configure: git config filter.dracon-assets.clean "python3 scripts/assets/filter-clean.py %f"
    """
    import os
    import sys
    
    sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    import common
    import s3
    
    MAX_BYTES = 524288000
    ALLOW = {"mp3", "ogg", "wav", "mp4", "mov", "webm", "png", "jpg", "jpeg",
             "webp", "onnx", "zip", "glb", "gltf", "ttf", "otf", "woff", "woff2",
             "trace.json", "gz"}
    QUARANTINE = "quarantine/doomtap"
    
    
    def main():
        rel = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else ""
        data = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
        if common.is_pointer(data):
            sys.stdout.buffer.write(data)
            return 0
        ext = rel.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].lower() if "." in rel else ""
        # multi-suffix (trace.json): try longest match
        cand = ".".join(rel.split(".")[-2:]).lower() if rel.count(".") >= 2 else ext
        ok_ext = cand if cand in ALLOW else (ext if ext in ALLOW else None)
        if not ok_ext or len(data) > MAX_BYTES:
            sys.stderr.write(f"dracon-assets: passthrough ({rel or '?'}): "
                             f"{'ext not managed' if not ok_ext else 'over 500MB cap'}\n")
            sys.stdout.buffer.write(data)
            return 0
        cfg = s3.load_config()
        if not cfg["access"] or not cfg["endpoint"]:
            sys.stderr.write("dracon-assets: no bucket credentials; storing bytes in git (L3 spill later)\n")
            sys.stdout.buffer.write(data)
            return 0
        import hashlib
        sha = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
        # Preserve promotion: if the manifest already pins this exact path+sha,
        # re-emit the existing pointer (assets/ stays assets/) instead of
        # demoting back to quarantine/ on every status/add. No upload needed
        # when the pinned object already exists; re-upload only when missing.
        try:
            man = common.load_manifest()
        except Exception:
            man = {"files": {}}
        prev = (man.get("files", {}) or {}).get(rel)
        if prev and prev.get("sha256") == sha and prev.get("object"):
            key = prev["object"]
            try:
                if s3.head(cfg, key) is None:
                    s3.put(cfg, key, data)
            except Exception as e:
                sys.stderr.write(f"dracon-assets: re-upload failed ({e}); storing bytes in git\n")
                sys.stdout.buffer.write(data)
                return 0
            sys.stdout.buffer.write(common.make_pointer(key, sha, len(data)))
            return 0
        key = common.object_key_for(QUARANTINE, sha, ok_ext)
        try:
            if s3.head(cfg, key) is None:
                s3.put(cfg, key, data)
        except Exception as e:
            sys.stderr.write(f"dracon-assets: upload failed ({e}); storing bytes in git\n")
            sys.stdout.buffer.write(data)
            return 0
        man = common.load_manifest()
        common.update_manifest_entry(rel, {"sha256": sha, "bytes": len(data),
                                           "object": key, "prefix": "quarantine"})
        sys.stdout.buffer.write(common.make_pointer(key, sha, len(data)))
        return 0
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        sys.exit(main())

    """git smudge filter: stdin=stored bytes, argv[1]=repo-relative path.
    
    - Non-pointer input -> pass through (plain git blobs keep working).
    - Pointer input -> fetch object, verify sha256, emit bytes.
    - Offline / missing object -> leave pointer bytes + loud stderr (build
      fails later with a clear 'run fetch-assets' message, never silently).
    Configure: git config filter.dracon-assets.smudge "python3 scripts/assets/filter-smudge.py %f"
    Required in .gitattributes per pattern, e.g.: *.mp3 filter=dracon-assets
    """
    import hashlib
    import os
    import sys
    
    sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    import common
    import s3
    
    
    def main():
        rel = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "?"
        data = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
        if not common.is_pointer(data):
            sys.stdout.buffer.write(data)
            return 0
        p = common.parse_pointer(data)
        if not p:
            sys.stderr.write(f"dracon-assets: corrupt pointer at {rel}; leaving as-is\n")
            sys.stdout.buffer.write(data)
            return 0
        cfg = s3.load_config()
        try:
            body = s3.get(cfg, p["object"])
        except Exception as e:
            body = None
            err = str(e)
        else:
            err = ""
        if body is None:
            sys.stderr.write(f"dracon-assets: cannot fetch {p['object']} for {rel} "
                             f"({err or 'missing'}); leaving pointer — run scripts/assets/fetch-assets.py\n")
            sys.stdout.buffer.write(data)
            return 0
        if hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest() != p["sha256"]:
            sys.stderr.write(f"dracon-assets: CORRUPT object {p['object']}; leaving pointer\n")
            sys.stdout.buffer.write(data)
            return 0
        sys.stdout.buffer.write(body)
        return 0
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        sys.exit(main())
